newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end higher, off peaks.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end higher, off peaks.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended moderately active pit trading higher but below price peaks.
Traders said turnover concentrated in the morning, with afternoon action slowing but marked by occasional spurts of business.
June marks briefly spiked up to the day's high after midday when a dealer bought and triggered buystops near the $0.5916 area.
Brokers said the rise occurred after players earlier failed to push the contract through sellstops they had expected to encounter on the downside.

Talk that a large hedge fund was selling Swiss francs and buying sterling circulated widely before midday, as sterling continued wending its way higher while Swiss franc eroded briefly to the minus side and the day's low.

But one floor chartist said he was impressed with June Swiss francs' ability to hold support at $0.6974, or 1.4392 spot. He said that resilience could point to some technical upside for the Swiss unit soon.
Sterling also continued to gain ground on crosses after its overseas rise premised on expectations that British interest rates are headed higher to dampen inflation.
The Bank of England's quarterly report said further monetary policy tightening was needed to hit the 2.5-percent inflation target in the medium term.
Futures showed muted reaction to U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's statement Tuesday that U.S. dollar policy remains unchanged. Brokers called the comment a reiteration.
"It's the same old (talk)," said one broker. "That's probably why the dollar didn't catch a bid."
Nor did currencies react much when U.S. debt and stock index futures expanded losses on a Reuters story that fed jitters that U.S. rates could rise by 25 basis points May 20.
